new_rng = ("    def _make_test_folds(self, X, y=None):\n"
           "        rng = check_random_state(self.random_state)\n")

           "        Whether to shuffle each stratification of the data before splitting\n"
           "        into batches.\n")
new_doc = ("    shuffle : boolean, optional\n"
           "        Whether to shuffle each class's samples before splitting into\n"
           "        batches. Note that the samples within each split will not be\n"
           "        shuffled.\n")
assert old_doc in s
s = s.replace(old_doc, new_doc)

old = '''        per_cls_cvs = [
            KFold(self.n_splits, shuffle=self.shuffle,
                  random_state=rng).split(np.zeros(max(count, self.n_splits)))
            for count in y_counts]

        test_folds = np.zeros(n_samples, dtype=np.int)

                # If this is the case, let's trim it:
                test_split = test_split[test_split < len(cls_test_folds)]
                cls_test_folds[test_split] = test_fold_indices
                test_folds[y == cls] = cls_test_folds
'''
new = '''        # Assign each sample to a test fold. Without shuffling, the samples
        # of a class are affected to the folds in a round-robin fashion, which
        # is equivalent to running KFold on the samples of that class.
        # With shuffling, the fold labels are permuted independently for each
        # class: a single RandomState instance is shared by all the classes so
        # that each class gets a different permutation (instead of the same
        # one applied to every class, which would only change the order of the
        # folds).
        test_folds = np.empty(n_samples, dtype=np.int)
        for k, cls in enumerate(unique_y):
            cls_test_folds = np.arange(y_counts[k]) % self.n_splits
            if self.shuffle:
                rng.shuffle(cls_test_folds)
            test_folds[y == cls] = cls_test_folds
'''
assert old in s
s = s.replace(old, new)

open(p, 'w').write(s)
print("patched")

import numpy as np
from sklearn.model_selection import StratifiedKFold

X = np.arange(20).reshape(-1, 1)
y = np.array([1] * 10 + [0] * 10)

def folds(shuffle, seed):
    skf = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=shuffle, random_state=seed)
    return [tuple(np.sort(te)) for _, te in skf.split(X, y)]

print("no-shuffle stable:", folds(False, 1) == folds(False, 2))
print("seeds differ:", folds(True, 1) != folds(True, 2))
print("repeatable:", folds(True, 1) == folds(True, 1))

# random_state as RandomState instance is accepted and advances state
rng = np.random.RandomState(0)
a = [tuple(t) for _, t in StratifiedKFold(3, shuffle=True, random_state=rng).split(X, y)]
b = [tuple(t) for _, t in StratifiedKFold(3, shuffle=True, random_state=rng).split(X, y)]
print("RandomState accepted, differs on reuse:", a != b)

# imbalanced classes / non-stratifiable edge case still works
yb = np.array([1] * 7 + [0] * 3)
for seed in (0, 1, 2):
    for tr, te in StratifiedKFold(3, shuffle=True, random_state=seed).split(X[:10], yb):
        assert set(tr).isdisjoint(set(te)) and len(tr) + len(te) == 10
print("imbalanced edge case OK")
